# Complexity AI

> We train AI scientists on real lab work. RL environments graded by real experiments, not opinions.

Website: https://www.complexity-ai.com/
Contact: contact@complexity-ai.com
Company: Complexity LLC
Mission: Bring autonomous science to every lab in the world.

## The Problem

AI knows biology but cannot yet judge experiments, and AI labs cannot train what they cannot grade. Models beat human experts on protocol quizzes (Anthropic, Oct 2025), but a quiz is not an experiment. In a Complexity AI test (2026), two stains failed in a real bone-marrow run: experts still found the cells, while Opus 5.5 found under half, twice. In blind runs, models found a subtle real effect and then declined to call it. Papers report results, not why an expert trusted a run or threw it out. Root cause: models learn what they are graded on, and nobody grades them on real experiments.

## Today: RL Environments

For frontier AI labs and RL environment vendors. Real lab tasks inside the software scientists use, built from raw instrument files plus the lab's measured result. Graders are tested on real outcomes and backed by a library of real failures. Families: cytometry, single-cell, assays, and imaging. An OT-2 instrument twin is a prototype. The task library holds 32 tasks today, with more each quarter.

## Next: Task Engine

Failures seen in paid analysis jobs and expert sessions are rebuilt as tasks on public data, with a planted change where needed. Each task has an answer key from independent evidence or known by design. Licenses or runs are bought only when a buyer orders.

## How the Loop Works

1. Discover: real failures found in paid analysis jobs and expert sessions with AI.
2. Rebuild: built on public data, with a planted change if needed and a real answer key.
3. Training: frontier labs and RL environment vendors train on the tasks.
4. Grading: graders find where models misjudge real data.
5. Next sessions: new sessions target where models still fail.
6. Harder tiers: solved tasks become regression tests; new work moves on.

## Roadmap (next 24 months; targets, not commitments)

- Today to 6 months: frontier packs rebuilt after every model release; expert sessions.
- 6 to 12 months: new environment families and private test sets; a failure library across instruments; a paid analysis service, confidential like any CRO, for research labs, CROs, and biotech teams; small error-check models.
- 12 to 24 months: instrument twins, OT-2 first (a prototype built from one robot's records exists today), then more instruments built from labs' own records; run-QC models trained on the failure map.

## OT-2 Twin (prototype)

An OT-2 twin built from one real robot's records: its calibrated tip lengths, labware offsets, and the depth where its tip touched a 2 mL tube. It runs a protocol in Opentrons' official 8.8.2 engine and checks every move against labware shapes from the official definitions before the robot runs it. It reproduces 5 of 5 recorded arc outcomes from the robot. On a test protocol with four bad moves, Opentrons' analysis returns OK and the twin reports five contacts, each tied to its script line; the protocol that ran on the robot has no findings. How one move is checked: a move is requested from a protocol line or by an agent through MCP; Opentrons' engine plans it with the robot's tip lengths and offsets; the twin places the tip along every planned segment; the path is checked against labware shapes from the official definitions, with wells kept hollow; the software result and the geometric finding are recorded separately and tied to the script line. A finding means the tip's path meets labware; it does not predict damage.

Task families in the twin: arc moves, probing toward a tube bottom without contact, stale offsets (proceed or defer), and measuring a rack's offset. Hidden setup stays hidden during evaluation.

Next for the twin: agent practice tested on new layouts, full tip and pipette shapes, supervised checks on the real robot, and more operations admitted one at a time.

The homepage shows a rendered replay. No live hardware is attached, and the replay does not certify physical safety.

## Customers and Partners

Design partners: Fleet and micro1. Fleet uses Complexity AI in its benchmarking product to run evaluations and investigate model failures. Complexity AI works with wet-lab experts at Arene Life Sciences and a CRO partner.
